requirements.title: Rich terminal UI with native cursor and responsive hierarchy
requirements.acceptance: Native block cursor, gutter hierarchy, visible reasoning, formatted content, panel layout and bounded streaming are deterministic and tested.

requirements.title: ContextPatch model editing protocol
requirements.acceptance: apply_patch accepts contextual add/update/delete/move operations without hunk counts, applies transactions safely and separates strict unified diffs.

requirements.title: Host-neutral patch tool pack
requirements.acceptance: TUI, Chrome and isolated workspaces share one PatchToolPack and ContextPatch semantics through narrow host adapters.

requirements.title: Versioning and requirement traceability
requirements.acceptance: Every new requirement has unique identity, linked design and test documents, a target version, and a traceable commit message enforced by tooling.

requirements.title: Repository-level agent instructions
requirements.acceptance: Repository-level AGENTS.md makes requirement, version, commit, verification and release rules mandatory for every coding agent.

requirements.title: Host capability ports and composable coding workspace
requirements.acceptance: Host adapters expose probeable narrow ports and named application actions; profiles and capability graphs compose host-neutral coding tool packs; unavailable applicable actions degrade explicitly and cannot produce false completion evidence; no generic exec, Python, shell or binary runner is built in.

requirements.title: Portable workspace capsule and cross-host continuity
requirements.acceptance: A versioned, integrity-checked workspace capsule transfers project content, agent sessions and tasks, VCS/Git state, artifacts, evidence and environment requirements; import is staged and atomic, running resources are reconciled, host-sensitive state stays out of the agent namespace, and evidence is invalidated when the environment changes.

requirements.title: Portable Git backend with Git-compatible repository format
requirements.acceptance: PortableGitBackend is the default host-independent Git implementation and supports the common local Git subset over a workspace filesystem without a git binary; its objects, refs, HEAD and index interoperate with standard Git, while the CLI backend remains optional for advanced operations and conformance testing.
